Can you experience the thrill of Rafting in Rishikesh for just ₹400? In this video, we share our real river rafting experience during our budget trip to Rishikesh.

We planned a budget-friendly trip to Rishikesh, but there was one adventure we simply couldn't miss: Rafting in Rishikesh, one of the most popular adventure activities in India.

I was travelling with my friend Sofiyan, and things got interesting even before the adventure began. We had forgotten to bring our shorts and T-shirts, so we had to buy them from a nearby shop before heading out for rafting.

We purchased our rafting tickets for approximately ₹400 per person and joined seven other people in our rafting boat. Before entering the river, our guide explained everything we needed to know, including how to paddle forward, reverse, stop, and navigate the rapid waves.

Then the real adventure began.

We covered approximately 12 kilometres of river rafting, surrounded by the beautiful natural scenery of Rishikesh. Every rapid brought a new thrill, and every moment became a memory worth keeping.

For safety reasons, our mobile phones and other electronic devices were packed away before the rafting started. Our guide captured the adventure using a GoPro, and we paid an additional ₹300 for the photos and videos.

Honestly, this was one of the most memorable experiences of our trip. If you're planning a budget trip to Rishikesh, river rafting is an adventure worth considering.

Rafting ticket: Approximately ₹400 per person
GoPro photos and videos: ₹300 extra
Shorts and T-shirts: Additional cost

In this Dhanushkodi Rameshwaram travel experience, we explore one of the most fascinating destinations in South India. Dhanushkodi is famous for its beautiful coastline, Dhanushkodi Beach, mysterious abandoned structures and fascinating Dhanushkodi history. Once a thriving town, Dhanushkodi was devastated by a cyclone in 1964 and is now popularly known as one of India's mysterious ghost towns.

Our journey continues through Rameshwaram, one of the most important pilgrimage and historical destinations in Tamil Nadu. If you're planning Rameshwaram travel or looking for places to visit in Rameshwaram, this destination offers a unique combination of spirituality, history, beaches and incredible landscapes.

We also visit the famous Pamban Bridge in Rameshwaram, an iconic landmark connecting Rameshwaram Island with mainland India. The historic Pamban railway bridge and the surrounding ocean views make this one of the most memorable experiences on a Tamil Nadu travel journey.

The region around Dhanushkodi is also closely associated with the legendary Ram Setu, also known as Adam's Bridge, making it an important destination for both history and mythology. From Dhanushkodi Beach and Rameshwaram to Pamban Bridge, this journey showcases some of the most beautiful and historical places in Tamil Nadu.

Welcome! I'm Gillian, and I've been working hard over the past decade to overcome a shopping addiction and learn to be content with less stuff.

- An occasional vlog

recent_videos.title: Sri Lanka Trip from India | Complete Travel Guide |  7-Day Itinerary | Full Plan Under ₹50,000?
recent_videos.description:
Planning a Sri Lanka trip? Stop — there are 4 things you need to know first.

Sri Lanka costs about the same as a Goa or Kerala trip, and Chennai to
Colombo is a flight of just 1 hour 20 minutes. It is the cheapest and
closest international trip you can take from India.

This video covers everything you need before you book — the right season,
the real cost, Sri Lanka's old connection with India, and the four
completely different ways to travel the island.

The biggest mistake people make is going to the wrong coast in the wrong
month. Sri Lanka has two separate monsoons running at opposite times of
year. So there is no bad time to visit Sri Lanka — only a wrong coast.


📍 WHAT'S COVERED
- South West vs North East — the right season for each coast
- South West Monsoon (May–Sep) and North East Monsoon (Nov–Mar)
- A realistic budget breakdown for the whole trip
- Sri Lanka's 8 UNESCO World Heritage Sites
- Cultural Circuit, Ramayana Trail, Wildlife and Beach circuits
- Chennai → Colombo — 686 km, 1 hour 20 minutes
- Full route: Colombo, Kandy, Sigiriya, Dambulla, Nuwara Eliya,
  Ella, Yala, Mirissa and Galle

🇱🇰 SRI LANKA — QUICK FACTS
- Length: 433 km (Point Pedro to Dondra Head)
- Width: 225 km at its widest point
- Area: 65,610 km²
- 8 UNESCO World Heritage Sites — 6 cultural, 2 natural
- Two monsoons, so one coast is always in season


Tell me in the comments: when are you going to Sri Lanka? 👇

There used to be a time when the dream was simple: get an education, find a good job, get married and have a family, buy a house, maybe get a dog.

The “normal” life.

But after debilitating headaches, I realized that if pushing yourself to the brink for a job was considered “normal,” then maybe normal wasn't for me anymore.

So since then, I’ve chosen to design my own life. One that's taken me from the Netherlands to Thailand, Bulgaria, Spain, and now soon back to Thailand again.

And today, I want to talk about why and how I did it.

When was the last time you did absolutely nothing?

We're constantly busy, connected. You may even feel guilty if you’re not being "productive" every minute of the day. But doing nothing isn’t a bad thing. When you give your mind and body a break, it has real benefits.

In the Netherlands, we have a word for doing nothing: it’s called niksen. 

In today’s video, I share what niksen is, why it matters, and a few simple ways you can practice it in your daily life.

🥾 Planning the Annapurna Base Camp Trek? 🇳🇵🏔️
Don’t make these 5 BIG mistakes!

These mistakes can make your ABC Trek harder, more stressful, and more expensive. 💸

• 01 | Carry enough Nepali cash 💰
Carry sufficient Nepali currency (NPR) because Indian currency may not work everywhere, and UPI is not available at every location in the mountains.

• 02 | Get your permits sorted beforehand 📄
Make sure you have all the required ABC Trek permits and documents before starting your trek to avoid getting stopped on the route.

• 03 | Stay hydrated 💧
Always carry drinking water. If you refill from natural water streams, use water purification tablets before drinking.

• 04 | Don’t overpack 🎒
Avoid unnecessary items. The heavier your backpack, the harder your trek will be!

• 05 | Carry protein & energy bars ⚡
Some trekking sections have shops far apart, so keep protein bars, energy bars and quick snacks for an instant energy boost.

recent_videos.description:

recent_videos.description:
Can you explore Srinagar in just 24 hours? What are the best things to do, places to visit, markets to explore and must try local food in just one day in Srinagar, Kashmir. 

So we started this 1 day in Srinagar challenge to explore the beautiful summer capital of Kashmir! From the stunning panoramic views at Astanmarg Viewpoint to a Shikara ride on Dal Lake, the historic lanes of Old Srinagar, and the lively atmosphere of Lal Chowk, this journey showed us different sides of the Srinagar city.

Srinagar is much more than its beautiful landscapes. It's about its people, local markets, historic architecture, peaceful lakes, and the everyday life that makes this city so special.

In this Srinagar vlog, join us as we explore:
Shalimar Garden/Shalimar Bagh - One of the most beautiful Mughal garden of Kashmir
Astanmarg Viewpoint – breathtaking views of Srinagar, highest point in Srinagar
Dal Lake – experiencing the city from a Shikara
Old Srinagar – exploring the historic streets and local life
Lal Chowk – discovering the heart of the city and the area which used to be very sensitive 
Floating vegetable market - the most unique experience in Srinagar
Local food - Cheese case, Walnut fudge, masala roti, Nadru and more
Meena bazar - a unique floating shopping mall of Srinagar
Is Srinagar Really as Beautiful as Everyone Says?

Is one day enough to explore Srinagar? Watch till the end and decide for yourself!

recent_videos.description:
क्या आप भी पढ़ाई तो करते हो, लेकिन कुछ समय बाद सब भूल जाते हो? 🥲📚

इस वीडियो में मैंने 3 ऐसी ट्रिक्स बताई हैं जिन्हें आप अपनी Daily Study Routine में शामिल कर सकते हैं।

📌 3 Best Memory Tricks:

1️⃣ Active Recall – किताब बंद करके याद करो कि आपने क्या पढ़ा।
2️⃣ Spaced Repetition – एक ही टॉपिक को सही अंतराल पर दोबारा रिवाइज करो।
3️⃣ Question Practice – पढ़ने के बाद सवाल हल करके अपनी तैयारी चेक करो।

अगर आप CET, SSC, UPSC, या किसी भी Government Exam की तैयारी कर रहे हैं, तो इन ट्रिक्स को अपनी पढ़ाई में जरूर अपनाएँ। ❤️

recent_videos.title: The Buy Nothing Rebellion: Seeing Through the Illusion
recent_videos.description:
Warriors,

Right now, millions of people are participating in the 'Buy Nothing Rebellion.' It’s a beautiful movement rooted in minimalism, practical frugality, saving money, reducing waste, and opting out of anti-consumerist traps.

But I'm taking it a bit deeper. 
I don’t just want to talk about the physical act of buying nothing. I want to talk about why I am choosing to buy INTO nothing.

In this video I use 3 deep ideas to explain:
1. Moving from the illusion of what we buy (The Empty Box)
2. To the identity we lose (The Dirty Mirror)
3. To the ultimate liberation of letting go (The Open Fist)

recent_videos.title: No Spend Month | Frugal Living from an Extreme Minimalist | I have saved thousands of dollars
recent_videos.description:
Warriors,
In this video, I share how I do a no-spend month- not just as a financial practice, but as a discipline of awareness. Beyond the practical habits, I speak about my mindset and perception that make a no-buy month natural and sustainable to do over months, if not an entire year. Doing this multiple times during the year, has saved me thousands of dollars, but the deeper reward has been far greater than money alone.

For me, a no-buy month is not an act of deprivation or a temporary challenge. It is a conscious step away from the endless noise of modern consumer culture — a culture designed to keep the mind restless, always chasing novelty, validation, and temporary satisfaction. Yet there is something powerful that happens when you learn to observe these impulses without immediately obeying them.

The reason I do a no spend month is to obviously save a tonne of money but it also allows me to find contentment in what I already have and in only having the essentials that a human being needs.

Money was invented to control us. Living frugally leads to saving money which leads to more options, and so, less control.

recent_videos.title: An Extreme Minimalist's 1 Minute Beauty Routine | Being Raw
recent_videos.description:
Warriors,
I show you all my extreme minimalist beauty routine. It has taken me years to get to this place of only using a few products and to be able to get in and out of the bathroom in one minute. This kind of minimalism is deeply in link with going down the spiritual path- to become aware of what Im putting on myself, see through the thousands of products there are out there, letting go of the need to impress others and not taking part in what society tells us is "normal" and what one "needs" to use to get ready and make oneself beautiful.

recent_videos.title: I stopped shaving everything | This is real beauty | Embracing being a human | Extreme Minimalism
recent_videos.description:
Warriors,
I have been shaving/waxing since I hit puberty at 12 years old. The classic reason being wanting to look like that hairless goddess we have all seen in advertisements, movies, pictures and everything around us telling us that this is what makes a woman look beautiful. Society made me feel like I was gross or even not taking care of myself if I didn't shave my armpits, legs, arms, upper-lips etc. The idea of what a beautiful woman in our society is toxic, and I'm going against it. One of the steps is to let my hair grow and embrace being a human being- which is, a matter of fact, a hairy creature (well, some more than others). Since I stopped shaving, I feel even closer to home- which is the real me. It aligns with my values and way of life, which is being a natural human being, a raw human being and an honest human being- if you see a woman or man out there with their hair being in its most natural state, they are to be admired and they are the ones who are truly beautiful.

recent_videos.description:
Singapore Changi Airport Complete Guide & Tour 🇸🇬 | Things to Do, Transit Areas & FREE City Tours

The Transit Area is the area after immigration/security where international passengers wait for their connecting or departing flights. If you are transiting through Singapore and do not clear immigration, you remain inside the transit area.

The Public Area is outside immigration and is accessible after you officially enter Singapore. This is where you can access places such as Jewel Changi Airport.

IMPORTANT: Jewel Changi Airport is located in the PUBLIC AREA. So, if you are a transit passenger and want to visit Jewel, you generally need to clear Singapore immigration and be eligible to enter Singapore. Make sure you have the required entry permission or visa before planning to leave the transit area. Jewel is directly connected to Terminal 1 and is located between Terminal 2 and Terminal 3.

The standard Canopy Park admission includes:

• Discovery Slides
• Foggy Bowls
• Petal Garden
• Topiary Walk

Additional paid attractions include:

• Mastercard Canopy Bridge
• Hedge Maze
• Mirror Maze
• Bouncing Net
• Walking Net

BOOK JEWEL & CANOPY PARK ATTRACTIONS:
https://www.klook.com/activity/25872-jewel-changi-airport-attractions-ticket-singapore/?spm=SearchResult.SearchResult_LIST&clickId=ed5afe9a66

Another amazing experience for people with a LONG LAYOVER is the FREE SINGAPORE TOUR! 🇸🇬🚌

Eligible transit passengers with a layover between approximately 5.5 and 24 hours can join a complimentary guided tour organised for transit passengers. The tours allow you to step outside the airport and experience parts of Singapore during your layover.

Passengers can pre-book one tour itinerary before their travel date or visit the Free Singapore Tour booths inside the Transit Area upon arrival, subject to seat availability.

recent_videos.title: FIFA Makes Millions Selling the Same Ticket 3 Times
recent_videos.description:
The FIFA World Cup 2026 hype is real: final match tickets are soaring up to ₹28 Lakh. But did you know FIFA earns from each ticket three times?

With their Triple Reward system, FIFA charges 15% commission from both the seller and buyer when tickets are resold on the official platform, while the seat was already sold once at the original price. Add dark patterns like countdown timers that pressure fans into buying expensive tickets quickly, and it becomes a masterclass in profit maximization at the expense of ethics.

German courts have now issued an injunction, and US Attorney Generals have started legal investigations. This video breaks down how FIFA is legally exploiting fans, why it matters, and the global reaction.

recent_videos.title: DIY Snowman Christmas Window Hanger ⛄ Popsicle Stick Craft
recent_videos.description:
Turn popsicle sticks, yarn, and a piece of blue cardstock into an adorable DIY Snowman Christmas Window Hanger! ⛄🎄✨

This handmade Christmas decoration features a miniature four-pane window, a snowy winter village backdrop, and a smiling yarn snowman sitting on a fluffy snow-covered ledge. Evergreen branches, red berries, a frosted pinecone, golden jingle bells, and rustic jute twine complete the cozy holiday look.

🎄 FROM POPSICLE STICKS TO A TINY CHRISTMAS WINDOW

Start with natural wooden craft sticks and a piece of blue cardstock for the background. Arrange the sticks into a rectangular frame, then add a vertical and horizontal crossbar to create four little windowpanes.

Secure a loop of jute twine to the top so the miniature Christmas window can hang on a wall or interior door.

The pale wood contrasts with the soft winter-blue background, creating a simple frame for a magical snow scene.

❄️ CREATE THE WINTER WONDERLAND BACKDROP

Inside the window, add a snowy village illustration with evergreen trees, gently falling snow, and tiny cottages glowing in the winter landscape.

The four-pane frame makes the picture look like a cozy view through a window on Christmas Eve.

Along the bottom edge, add fluffy white cotton to resemble a blanket of fresh snow. This soft foreground adds dimension and gives the snowman a place to sit.

⛄ MEET THE LITTLE YARN SNOWMAN

The centerpiece is a miniature snowman made from white yarn, with black bead eyes, a tiny orange carrot nose, rosy cheeks, and a friendly smile.

A deep red knitted pom-pom hat and a forest-green scarf give the character a classic Christmas color palette. Two small wooden buttons decorate the front of the white yarn body.

The snowman’s legs are made from dangling pieces of natural twine, finished with round wooden beads for feet.

Place the snowman on the fluffy snow ledge so its little legs hang below the window frame. That tiny dangling-feet detail gives this ornament so much personality!

recent_videos.title: DIY Santa Claus Rope Wreath 🎅 Turn Cotton Rope Into Christmas Decor!
recent_videos.description:
Turn an ordinary cardboard ring and soft cotton rope into an adorable DIY Santa Claus Christmas wreath! 🎅🎄✨ This handmade Santa face door hanger combines fluffy white rope loops, a red velvet Santa hat, a cheerful face, and a festive bow with a gold jingle bell.

The finished wreath looks beautiful against a red door, making it a playful idea for Christmas wall decor, holiday entryways, and rustic handmade decorations.

🎄 FROM CARDBOARD RING TO CHRISTMAS WREATH

Start with a sturdy circular cardboard wreath base and a length of thick cream-colored cotton rope. Fold the rope into even loops and attach each loop around the outer edge of the ring. Continue working around the circle until the frame is covered in soft, petal-like rope loops.

The layered cotton rope creates a textured, almost snowflake-like silhouette. The open center of the cardboard ring becomes a natural place for Santa’s smiling face, transforming simple craft supplies into a recognizable Christmas character.

☺️ MAKE SANTA’S HAPPY FACE

Create a round, neutral-colored face piece and add little black eyes, white eyebrows, rosy pink cheeks, and a round wooden nose. Attach a fluffy white mustache and beard to bring Santa’s expression to life.

The soft white details contrast with the warm face color and rope texture, giving the handmade decoration a sweet, friendly look. Santa’s face sits inside the wreath like a portrait framed by loops of cream cotton rope.

🎅 ADD THE CLASSIC RED SANTA HAT

Dress the top of the face with a deep red Santa hat, a soft white fluffy brim, and a matching white pom-pom. Let the hat lean to one side for a playful holiday silhouette.

The bold red fabric adds instant Christmas color, while the fluffy trim makes the Santa character look cozy and festive. Combined with the cream rope frame, the design feels both rustic and cheerful.

recent_videos.description:
AGOMONI | A Home Shaped by Migration, Memory & Craftsmanship

What does it mean to create a home that carries the memories of one place while embracing the identity of another?

Introducing Agomoni, a residence in Kolkata designed by Envisage Architects for a Marwari family whose story is deeply rooted in both Rajasthan and Bengal.

More than a home, Agomoni is an exploration of cultural identity, belonging, and the beauty of Indian craftsmanship. The reds of Rajasthan meet the greens of Bengal, Shekhawati craftsmanship finds its place alongside Kalighat art, and traditional techniques are reimagined through a contemporary design language.

At the heart of the project lies the idea of process-driven luxury where luxury is not defined by excess, but by the time, skill, patience, and human effort invested in creating something meaningful.

From a handcrafted palanquin that took six months to complete and intricate stone inlay to commissioned artworks, traditional murals, and handwoven textiles, every detail tells a story of the people, places, and traditions that shaped it.

Agomoni is not a home that simply attempts to look Indian. It is a home that celebrates India as a collection of histories, cultures, crafts, and journeys.

A story of migration and memory. Of inheritance and reinvention. Of craftsmanship and belonging.

Welcome to Agomoni.

Stay tuned as we unveil the spaces, stories, and craftsmanship behind this home.

recent_videos.description:
What does it take to design a home in another country while staying true to your own design identity?

In this episode of In Hindsight, Meena and Vishal take you behind the scenes of our Singapore project, reflecting on the experiences, challenges, and learnings of designing and executing a home beyond borders.

From conducting due diligence and collaborating closely with the client to navigating local regulations, material sourcing, technical specifications, and execution processes, this project was as much about understanding a new country as it was about bringing a design vision to life.

We discuss why detailed documentation becomes crucial when working internationally, how technology helped us bridge geographical distances, and why involving local contractors early in the design process made all the difference.

But perhaps our biggest takeaway was this, Designing globally doesn't mean compromising on your identity.

We can retain our inherent Indian aesthetic sensibilities while working seamlessly with global processes and expertise.

Because the new India is unabashedly individualistic, yet very much globally relevant.

Join us as we look back at what it really takes to make a design process travel.

An Indian Home in Singapore | A Contemporary Bengali Home by Envisage Architects
recent_videos.description:
Sindhuparer Bari, meaning The Home Beyond the Seas, is a Bengali home in Singapore designed by Envisage for a family that has spent nearly two decades building a life abroad while remaining deeply connected to its roots.

Rather than recreating Kolkata or creating a nostalgic version of India, Envisage explored what it means to be Bengali in a contemporary global setting. The result is an Indian home in Singapore where culture is expressed through art, craftsmanship, materials, heirlooms, memories and everyday rituals.

Warm timber, handcrafted details, natural textures and rich terracotta tones create a sense of permanence and familiarity. Bengali art becomes an integral part of the interiors, from an original Jamini Roy in the foyer to a commissioned Mahishasura Mardini by Prasun Mazumdar in the living room, alongside Kalighat paintings and a work by Jogen Chowdhury.

The home also carries the family's memories forward. Heirloom furniture, existing cabinets, collected objects and treasured artefacts from their previous home were restored and carefully integrated into the new interiors. These pieces make the new house feel less like a departure and more like an evolution of a home already lived and loved.

Much of the home's soul travelled from India to Singapore. Indian floor tiles, bespoke lighting, handcrafted furniture, wallpapers, soft furnishings, artworks and accessories were sourced, commissioned and developed in India before finding their place within this Singapore residence.

In a city known for its pace, precision and efficiency, Sindhuparer Bari embraces a slower idea of living: permanence over novelty, craftsmanship over spectacle, and emotional connection over trends.
This is not simply an Indian interior in Singapore. It is a home about belonging.

A home where memories travel.
Where culture adapts without disappearing.
And where identity feels at home, wherever in the world that may be.

name: fayefilms
description:
Created in July 2020, fayefilms is a Youtube channel that produces videos about academics, effective study tips, productivity and occasionally art. 

As a Malaysian teen and student, Faye Ng found it difficult to find local role models whom she can learn from and relate to. Most Youtubers providing study tips in Malaysia are either much older or create content in other languages besides English.

Inspired by ‘Studytubers’ and ‘Studygrammers’ who go to the most prestigious universities in the UK and US, Faye decided to step up and be a creator too.

Thus, fayefilms was born, and its mission is to serve as a platform where all students are included, empowered and understood.

I’m also sharing a small Temu decor haul, including crystal candle holders, floating lotus flowers and pearl fairy lights.

You don’t need to buy everything new each year—a little rearranging and creativity can make familiar pieces feel special again. ❤️

Nearly six months ago I got laid off from my "full time freelance" role at a media industry that I had come to rely on for most of my income. But my career had been rocky for about a year before that as well. The media industry has changed so much with AI and the general population's preference for social media over reading articles and I allowed that to kind of sour my worldview.

I applied for full time jobs. I considered half a dozen career pivots. I thought finding a full time 9-5 office job in a North American city was the answer. But after almost securing a full time role, I realized I'm not ready to give up on my freelance career and building my personal brand. This is what I'm doing instead!

recent_videos.title: pros and cons of living in a studio apartment | my solo life in 200 sqft 🧸
recent_videos.description:
I absolutely love studio apartment living and I think even most of the cons can be pros if you have the right mindset and approach. Studio living, for me, is more sustainable and less overwhelming; it's more affordable, and I feel really safe and cozy living alone and starting over in my thirties. This video is what I love about it and how my studios have differed over the last four years in Montreal, Halifax, and Istanbul.

11:30 making the space feel homey and not like a liminal space
14:20 studios are small. make a life outside of your unit to thrive
16:30 it's hard to host people (but not impossible)
17:50 true con: your entire apartment smells like what you're cooking
19:15 there are way more pros and cons, and ways to turn cons into pros if you're creative!!

recent_videos.description:

recent_videos.title: No new outfit feels as good as being debt free #minimalism #debtfree
15 Things your wardrobe doesn’t need #minimalism #decluttering
recent_videos.description:
**15 things your wardrobe doesn’t need:**

1. Clothes you haven't worn in a year (12 months)
2. Duplicate items you don’t wear
3. Clothes that don't fit
4. Trendy pieces you don't really like
5. Shoes that hurt your feet
6. Items you're keeping only for sentimental reasons (store them in a memory box, rather than your daily wardrobe)
7. Fabrics that are high-maintenance and inconvenient to you
8. Clothes that are very worn out (stretched out, shrunk in the wash, holes in)
9. Clothes that still have tags on
10. Formal wear you don't need
11. Clothes that don’t match your current lifestyle
12. Gifts you never liked or wore
13. Clothes that make you feel insecure or uncomfortable
14. Clothes you’re keeping only because they cost a lot but don’t wear (sunk cost fallacy)
15. Excessive loungewear (there’s only so many pjs we need)

recent_videos.title: Just a mom in her 30s in her decluttering era #minimalism
recent_videos.description:
The 5️⃣ things that I wish I knew before I started decluttering:

1️⃣ Decluttering means there will be less tidying or laundry to do. Less stuff to move around when cleaning surfaces.

2️⃣ Toys will become more manageable and kids play better in a clutter-free environment.

3️⃣ It’s easier to find things when you need them, if they are not hidden behind piles of stuff in bursting wardrobes.

4️⃣ I enjoy wearing my clothes more now that I keep less. Because everything in my wardrobe fits me, makes me feel good and feels like me, not a “pinterest-perfect” version of me.

5️⃣ Decluttering saves you money. You spend less on random items that bring no value to your life.

.
#simplehome #decluttering #minimalism

You can start by trying to declutter 10 minutes every day for 30 days.

It’s also going to help you focus on just a really small spot in your home. It might be a kitchen drawer, your under-bed area, or a bedside table.

recent_videos.title: The Ancient Art of Turning Wax Into Metal | Meet Anil Baghmare
recent_videos.description:
This festive season, discover the timeless beauty of Dokra, through the work of State Award-winning artist Anil Baghmare.

For Anil, the journey with Dokra wasn’t always a straight one. He explored different fields and kinds of work over the years, but eventually found his way back to the craft he truly loved. With years of practice and dedication, he has built a deep understanding of this traditional metal-casting art form.

Dokra is made using the lost-wax casting technique, where every piece begins by hand. The form is first shaped in wax, with intricate patterns and details carefully added to its surface. It is then covered with layers of clay and heated, allowing the wax to melt away and leave behind a mould. Molten metal is poured into this mould and, once cooled, the clay is broken open to reveal the cast piece.

The final stages involve cleaning, refining and finishing the metal by hand. Since the clay mould is broken to release the artwork, each Dokra piece is unique, carrying subtle variations that are part of the craft itself.

Through his work, Anil continues to practise and preserve this traditional technique while giving it his own artistic expression.

Because building wealth isn’t always about earning more. Sometimes, it’s about managing what you already have with more discipline and intention.

In Japan, financial stability is often connected with simplicity, patience, discipline, mindful living, and smart spending. These ideas can help you reduce unnecessary expenses, control impulse buying, and make better financial decisions without giving up everything you enjoy.

Why is saying “NO” so difficult? And why do we keep saying YES when we actually want to say NO?

Do you agree to extra work when you’re already exhausted?
Do you lend money even when you’re uncomfortable?
Do you say YES to plans you don’t really want because you’re afraid someone might feel bad?
Do you stay quiet when someone crosses a line because you don’t want conflict?

If you often put other people’s needs, expectations and feelings before your own, you may be caught in a people-pleasing pattern.

Being kind, helpful and considerate isn’t the problem. The problem begins when your YES comes from fear, guilt, or the fear of disappointing someone, even when you genuinely want to say NO.

Over time, people-pleasing can leave you feeling mentally exhausted, frustrated, resentful, and disconnected from your own needs.

recent_videos.title: DJI Osmo Pocket 4 Unboxing: My First Ever Vlogging Camera
recent_videos.description:
DJI Osmo Pocket 4 Unboxing: My First Ever Vlogging Camera

There was a time I used to film my dreams on a phone with a cracked screen and a full heart.

Today, I finally unboxed my first ever vlogging camera, the DJI Osmo Pocket 4.

I’m not going to lie, my hands were shaking a little while opening the box. Not because of the camera, but because of everything it stands for. All the late nights, the doubts, the “log kya kahenge”, the days when I almost quit. And somehow I kept showing up.

This camera is not just a gadget for me. It’s proof that small beginnings are still beginnings.

In this video, I unbox it, show you what’s inside, and share my honest first impressions. And yes, you’ll see me smiling like a kid the whole time, because I genuinely couldn’t stop.

If you are also someone sitting in a small town with a big dream, this one’s for you. You don’t need everything to start. You just need to start.

Thank you for being part of this journey with me. Every view, every comment, every bit of love got me here. I promise to keep making things that feel real.

Watch till the end, and tell me in the comments: what’s that one thing you’re saving up for, or dreaming about?

Love,
Bawa
Sukoon with Bawa

recent_videos.title: I Was Invited as Guest Speaker to My Own School Army Public School Fazilka
recent_videos.description:
I studied at Army Public School Fazilka my whole life. Every morning in that uniform, every corner of that campus, every teacher who believed in me before I believed in myself. That school made me who I am.

So when the Army Brigade invited me to speak to its students, I didn’t know how to feel. The same school where I once sat and listened was now asking me to share my story with its children.

I talked about social media, about how it can change your life if you use it with purpose. But more than that, I wanted those kids to know that a boy from a small city like Fazilka can dream big too.

Some moments you don’t just remember, you feel them forever. This was one of them.

Thank you, Army Public School Fazilka. For everything. ❤️

It features four stunning cascades: Raja, Rani, Roarer, and Rocket. During the monsoon, this natural wonder becomes an unforgettable sight! 🌿💦
